NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Monday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over the country’s economic situation, saying that while Prime Minister Narendra Modi claims “all is well”, the reality on the ground is marked by soaring prices and shrinking incomes."The PM keeps saying सब चंगा सी (all is well), but actually सब महँगा सी (everything is expensive)," Ramesh said in a post on X.Highlighting the pressure on household budgets, Congress MP Ramesh cited the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), writing, "Official data just released shows that for four consecutive months now the WPI (Wholesale Price Index) inflation has been hovering around 10%. Prices of all essential commodities have continued their upward rise causing huge hardships to crores of families."Ramesh further cited findings by the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) to highlight the distress in the labour market, particularly in rural areas."To compound the misery, according to CMIE data, inflation-adjusted wages have also been consistently falling with a 5.7% drop since April. Rural India has seen a massive 9% decline - even in nominal terms, rural wages have fallen," Ramesh stated.Ramesh’s remarks came after the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for all commodities stood at 110.8 in August 2026, with annual wholesale inflation rising to 9.92 per cent year-on-year (YoY), according to official data released by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.The figure marked a marginal increase from July 2026, when headline wholesale inflation stood at 9.78 per cent. The all-commodities index also edged up from 110.0 recorded in the previous month.The rise reflected price pressures across major industrial and energy segments. Fuel and power recorded the sharpest increase, with YoY inflation accelerating to 22.93 per cent in August from 20.05 per cent in July.In contrast, inflation in primary articles moderated to 7.76 per cent from 8.52 per cent in the preceding month. Inflation in manufactured products edged up to 8.37 per cent from 8.29 per cent over the same period.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh launched a sharp attack on the Centre over the country’s economic situation. He said that while Prime Minister Narendra Modi claims “all is well”, the reality on the ground is marked by soaring prices and shrinking incomes.

Article Title: 'Ban defectors from public office': CJP backs Kapil Sibal's call for ban on MPs, MLAs who switch parties
Article Text:
Ban defectors from public office: CJP backs Kapil Sibal's anti-defection proposal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Monday endorsed senior advocate and Rajya Sabha member Kapil Sibal's proposal to bar MPs and MLAs who defect from their political parties from holding public office. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke described the proposal as the "need of the hour".Sibal, speaking at a talk titled 'Horse Trade and Democracy' in Kerala's Kochi, called for amendments to the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution to prevent party mergers from becoming "loopholes for mass walkouts".Under the existing law, legislators who defect are protected from disqualification if at least two-thirds of the members of their legislative party cross over to another party, with the move being treated as a merger.Sibal called for changes to the Tenth Schedule to close this "loophole" and ensure that "a merger is a merger of political parties and not a collective walkout by legislators".CJP co-convener Saurav Das backed Sibal's proposal, saying it was in line with the forum's first demand charter."Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal's proposal to ban any MP and MLA who gets elected on Party X's symbol and later defects to Party Y for money or under pressure should be welcomed.He calls for a 10-year ban," he said.Das said point 5 of CJP's first demand charter, released by Dipke, proposed an even stricter provision: barring defectors from holding any public office or contesting elections for 20 years."Breaking political parties, bribing MPs with 50-100 crore, toppling governments is a fraud committed on the country. Such fraud should never happen. The Anti-Defection law is outdated. The ruling party has ensured its misuse in its lust for eternal power. The young will change this," he said.Dipke reiterated the demand, calling it the "need of the hour". In a post on X, he said, "Any elected representative who switches parties after being elected should be barred from holding public office."The call for changes to the anti-defection law comes amid the ongoing political developments within the Trinamool Congress in the Lok Sabha and West Bengal Assembly.In the Lok Sabha, 20 of the TMC's 28 MPs have announced that they are leaving the party to form a separate Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), while extending support to the BJP-led NDA.The move has brought renewed attention to the anti-defection law and its two-thirds merger provision.In West Bengal, the faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee has sought recognition as the TMC and staked claim to the party's name, organisational control, assets and election symbol. The faction has also claimed the support of a majority of the party's newly elected MLAs.The Election Commission has begun examining the competing claims of the Ritabrata and Mamata Banerjee factions.The developments have focused attention on the Tenth Schedule provision that protects legislators from disqualification when two-thirds of a legislature party is deemed to have merged with another political party.The TMC developments come after seven Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha members joined the BJP earlier this year, with the group also invoking the two-thirds merger provision.The issue has also featured prominently in earlier splits involving the Shiv Sena and the Nationalist Congress Party in Maharashtra.In 2022, Eknath Shinde led a majority of Shiv Sena MLAs away from Uddhav Thackeray, triggering a change of government. In 2023, Ajit Pawar split the NCP and joined the BJP-led government along with a group of party legislators.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) backs Kapil Sibal's proposal to bar MPs and MLAs who defect from their political parties from holding public office. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke described the proposal as the "need of the hour" Sibal called for amendments to the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.

Article Title: Selfie crowds in mind, Delhi Urban Arts Commission seeks wider path around proposed CP artwork
Article Text:
The Delhi Urban Arts Commission reviewed a proposed artwork for Connaught Place's Central Park (File Photo)

The proposal is conceptually suitable but needs formal approval after revisions.





NEW DELHI: The installation of a proposed artwork at Connaught Place’s Central Park may have to make more room for potential admirers and selfie enthusiasts.Delhi Urban Arts Commission (DUAC), which foresees that crowds will gather at the installation site, has asked Mohan Foundation, which proposed the artwork, that the pathway leading to it should be widened from four feet to seven feet.The commission examined the artwork at the conceptual stage and did not approve the proposal at its Dec 26, 2024, meeting. It made several observations and later reviewed the submission along with the replies, drawings, photographs and other documents sent in by the architect, Tarun Walecha.The commission’s biggest concern was the space around the artwork. Mohan Foundation had proposed a green buffer space of about two feet to four feet around the art installation. Since visitors are likely to gather around the installation and stop for selfies, the commission suggested removing the green buffer area and widening the paved pathway to about seven feet.The commission, in its Dec 2024 minutes, described the installation as an art piece that would have a main structure, base, overhangs and a sphere with the heart. The minutes also referred to a triangular ceiling frame and noted that the structure would be sloping in nature.The commission also sought clearer details from Mohan Foundation on the material palette of the piece, how the structure would be fixed to the ground, its lighting and the use of solar panels.In its latest examination, the commission also flagged the arrangement of planters and vegetation on both sides of the pathway. It asked the architect to provide suitable openings at appropriate points so that visitors are able to move in and out, so that crowds can be managed better in one of Delhi’s busiest public spaces.The commission has also asked the architect to rework and coordinate the entire submission, including plans, elevations, 3D views and other drawings, and bring it back at the formal stage.In a recent meeting of the commission in Aug, the proposal was found to be conceptually suitable, provided the commission’s observations are incorporated. However, this does not amount to a formal approval. It will be reassessed at the formal stage against the commission’s 20-point criteria and will also require statutory approval of the local body concerned under Section 12 of the DUAC Act, 1973.
Article Summary: Delhi Urban Arts Commission (DUAC) has asked Mohan Foundation, which proposed the artwork, that the pathway leading to it should be widened from four feet to seven feet. The commission examined the artwork at the conceptual stage and did not approve the proposal at its Dec 26, 2024, meeting.

Article Title: Goods seized? Street vendors to get memos in Delhi
Article Text:
The court acted on a PIL connected to MCD and NDMC‘s seizure of goods from street vendors who violate rules.





NEW DELHI: Delhi High Court has asked MCD and NDMC to issue seizure memos to street vendors within 24 hours of confiscating their goods, and to videograph the entire process.In a recent order, a bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Vikas Mahajan specified that the seizure memos should mention the date of the seizure, a list of goods taken away, shelf numbers where they are kept, penalty or fine, if any, which is to be paid and the details of the officer who did the seizure.The court acted on a PIL connected to MCD and NDMC‘s seizure of goods from street vendors who violate rules.The petitioner organisation, Rehri Patri Ekta Manch, said that whenever such seizures are done, no memo is prepared by MCD or NDMC and the list of goods seized is also not given to the vendors. Only a receipt for the fine is issued in the evening after the seizure is done, the plea said.The civic agencies said the usual process is that the seizure is done at a particular point and if the officials prepare the seizure memo on the spot, other vendors get to know about it and they escape the seizure despite committing violations.Keeping this in mind, the seizure is first done, and in the evening a seizure memo is prepared along with the fine receipt and handed to the vendors, the counsel said.NDMC also said a warehouse is maintained by the authorities for storing the seized goods.When the vendor pays the fine, the goods are released to him, the counsel for the agency said, adding that videography or photography of the seizure are also done, depending upon the available resources.The court stressed that both MCD and NDMC are expected to follow Section 19 of the Street Vendors (Protection of livelihood and regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.“Accordingly, considering the difficulties expressed by the authorities... MCD and NDMC are permitted to issue seizure memos, in accordance with law within an outer limit of 24 hours from the seizure,” it said.
Article Summary: The court acted on a PIL connected to MCD and NDMC’s seizure of goods from street vendors who violate rules. The petitioner organisation, Rehri Patri Ekta Manch, said no memo is prepared by MCD or NDMC and the list of goods seized is also not given to the vendors.

Article Title: On 26th b’day, Saudi Arabia-based YouTuber pays for followers’ feast
Article Text:
YouTuber Anurag Dwivedi





LUCKNOW: Almost a year after the Enforcement Directorate registered a case against Saudi Arabia-based YouTuber Anurag Dwivedi and seized property in his hometown of Unnao, claiming it was amassed through unlawful means, the social media influencer celebrated his 26th birthday on Sunday in style.Dwivedi asked his followers to visit select eateries in Unnao and Nawabganj, enjoy a meal in his name and leave the bill to him.Describing it as a birthday celebration, he thanked his followers for their support. The cricket content creator has more than seven million YouTube subscribers and 2.4 million Instagram followers.Dwivedi posted a video on social media from Saudi Arabia around 12.30 pm, announcing that anyone could walk into several eateries in Unnao and eat for free.His message was simple: “Eat in my name, I’ll pay the bill.”The announcement quickly drew crowds at some of the participating outlets in Unnao and Nawabganj, with people queuing up to avail themselves of the offer.He named a few food outlets where people could enjoy dosa, ‘chhole-bhature’, samosa or pizza.Beginning his video with religious slogans, Dwivedi said he had turned 26 and wanted to celebrate not only with people in Nawabganj and Unnao but with people across the country.He said that even travellers on the Lucknow-Kanpur highway could take advantage of the offer at participating outlets.Towards the end of the video, he said completing 26 years in ‘Kalyug’ was itself a major achievement. He thanked his followers, expressed his affection for them and signed off with ‘Love you’ and ‘Jai Mata Ki’. The video was shared by his relatives and friends on social media.A resident of Nawabganj, around 27 km from the Unnao district headquarters, Dwivedi has built a substantial social media following. His online content largely revolves around cricket and cricketers, and he has also been associated with the online fantasy sports and gaming ecosystem.He made headlines last year after marrying his Lucknow-based girlfriend aboard a cruise in Dubai on Nov 22, 2025.The ED’s money laundering case against Dwivedi stems from a 2022 online betting racket busted in Siliguri, West Bengal.Five alleged supervisors of a betting syndicate operating through Telegram channels and platforms such as Skyexchange were arrested, and investigators identified Badal Bhardwaj as the alleged mastermind.As investigators tracked the money trail, they found transactions linked to accounts held by Dwivedi’s relatives and associates, prompting the ED to initiate a money laundering probe.The agency alleges that proceeds from illegal betting apps were routed through mule accounts and hawala networks into companies and family accounts linked to Dwivedi without any legitimate business basis.The probe led to searches across Lucknow, Unnao, Delhi, Mumbai, Surat and Varanasi in late 2025 and early 2026.During the raids, the ED seized luxury vehicles, including a Lamborghini Urus, Mercedes, BMW Z4, Ford Endeavour and Mahindra Thar, recovered around Rs 20 lakh in cash, and froze bank deposits, insurance policies and other assets.Officials also claimed to have found evidence of hawala transactions and investments in Dubai real estate.ED froze or attached assets worth between Rs 20 crore and Rs 23.7 crore. A prosecution complaint has already been filed before the Special PMLA Court in Kolkata.
Article Summary: Anurag Dwivedi asked his followers to visit select eateries in Unnao and Nawabganj, enjoy a meal in his name and leave the bill to him. The cricket content creator has more than seven million YouTube subscribers and 2.4 million Instagram followers.

Article Title: Alandi Temple: After Mula, mass fish kill spotted in Indrayani river near Alandi temple
Article Text: PUNE: Days after dead fish were found floating in Mula river, a similar mass fish kill was spotted in Indrayani river near Alandi temple, raising fresh concerns over the region’s spiralling river pollution.The dead fish were discovered just meters away from Alandi temple, a prominent pilgrimage site that draws hundreds of thousands of devotees from across Maharashtra. Environmental activists stated that such incidents have become alarmingly frequent, alleging that local authorities have failed to curb illegal discharge of pollutants into the water.Prashant Raul of Green Army environmental group spotted the dead fish during a visit to the riverside on Saturday. He noted that despite reporting similar incidents to the authorities in the past, no concrete improvements have been made.“Untreated effluent entering from Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) limits through Ram Zara nullah, combined with sewage from upstream villages, is the primary driver of pollution in Indrayani,” Raul said.Raul emphasised that fish deaths are particularly concerning during the monsoon season.Increased water flow from dam releases typically prevents stagnant conditions associated with such die-offs. He added that the foul odour emanating from the river has become so severe that standing near the banks is now difficult for pilgrims and residents alike.The latest ecological crisis follows a comprehensive three-year research study that flagged a severe and persistent deterioration in Indrayani’s water quality. The study, conducted between 2022 and 2024 by PhD scholar Kiran Ghotkule and his colleagues, analysed the river across various stretches.The scientific assessment revealed a stark upstream-to-downstream degradation. While upstream testing stations recorded “good” water quality—maintaining a water quality index (WQI) below 50—downstream stretches consistently plummeted into “very poor/unsafe” category, with WQI levels breaching the 250–300 mark.According to the study, critically high levels of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) and chemical oxygen demand (COD), alongside heavy nitrate enrichment and critically low dissolved oxygen, indicate severe eutrophcation in the lower reaches.The research identified the root causes as untreated domestic sewage, agricultural runoff, and toxic industrial effluents originating from Talegaon-Chakan-Pimpri-Chinchwad industrial belt.
Article Summary: The dead fish were discovered just meters away from Alandi temple, a prominent pilgrimage site that draws hundreds of thousands of devotees. Environmental activists stated that such incidents have become alarmingly frequent, alleging that local authorities have failed to curb illegal discharge of pollutants into the water.

Article Title: Haryana clears Rs 9,700cr road projects, including five bypasses
Article Text:
Rs 9,700-crore road investment cleared in Haryana (AI image used for representational purpose only)





GURGAON: Haryana has approved a Rs 9,700-crore road infrastructure package that includes bypasses around five cities and a policy for developing ring roads and national highways outside cities and towns with populations above one lakh.The projects are aimed at diverting through traffic from urban areas and easing congestion on national highways passing through or near built-up areas.Chief minister Nayab Singh Saini approved the projects at a meeting to finalise the financial model for the state’s contribution to road projects being taken up under the master plan for decongesting urban stretches of national highways.The approved projects include the Hisar, Kurukshetra-Ladwa, Narnaul, Jind and Sohna-Palwal bypasses.The nearly 11-km Narnaul city bypass will connect to NH-148B. At Jind, an outer ring road and a four-lane bypass on NH-352 have been approved. The Palwal-Sohna bypass from NH-919 will be redesigned and upgraded to a four-lane road over about 24 km.The Hisar bypass will connect the Hisar-Rajgarh road (NH-52) with the Hisar-Delhi and Hisar-Kaithal roads. The DPR for the Kurukshetra-Ladwa bypass has been prepared, with work expected to begin soon.The state government will also formulate a policy for developing outer ring roads and national highways in line with the Centre’s policy framework. A three-member committee comprising officials from the finance, public works and urban local bodies departments has been formed to work out Haryana’s share of the cost under the Centre-state funding arrangement.The state also plans greenfield connectivity linking the DND-Faridabad-Ballabhgarh-KMP corridor and Delhi-Mumbai Expressway with Jewar International Airport.The land share for the Karnal ring road has been deposited, while construction of the ring road connecting Ambala City and Ambala Cantonment is underway.The meeting also cleared a railway underbridge on Civil Station Road in Sirsa on the Rewari-Bathinda railway line and several link-road works in Mahendragarh and adjoining areas.
Article Summary: The projects are aimed at diverting through traffic from urban areas and easing congestion on national highways passing through or near built-up areas. The approved projects include the Hisar, Kurukshetra-Ladwa, Narnaul, Jind and Sohna- Palwal bypasses.

Article Title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to former employee who resigned 'warning' that AI could kill all of us, says: I agree with Jacob Coxon on ...
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

What did Jacob Coxon say about AI killing humans

Dario Amodei says he agrees with Jacob Coxon

Why Dario Amodei does not give one AI extinction percentage

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has responded to former researcher Jacob Coxon’s resignation, who left the AI company earlier this month and warned that rapidly developing AI systems could “kill us all by the end of the decade. ” In a CNN interview, Dario Amodei said he “agree[s] with Jacob much more than I disagree with him”, while making clear that Coxon was not specifically accusing Anthropic of acting irresponsibly. Instead, Amodei said Jacob Coxon was warning about the wider AI industry moving too fast. During the interview, Dario Amodei also explained why he no longer prefers giving a single percentage for the risk of AI causing catastrophic harm, saying the focus should be on choosing the right path for AI development.Jacob Coxon, who worked on pretraining research at both Anthropic and OpenAI, resigned from Anthropic earlier this month. In a post on X, he said the companies were not acting responsibly and warned that the AI industry was moving towards self-improving superintelligence.Coxon wrote that AI developers were “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” He also said people building AI “earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”His post quickly drew widespread attention, with CNN reporting that it was seen by more than 40 million people.Asked by CNN's Anderson Cooper whether he believes AI could kill all humans and what probability he would put on that outcome, Amodei did not reject Coxon's concern.“It's funny, I agree with Jacob much more than I disagree with him,” Amodei said.He then explained why he viewed Coxon's resignation differently from a direct criticism of Anthropic.“It's an interesting resignation, because when he left, he said, you know, I think Anthropic is the most responsible player, right? I think Anthropic is the most aware of these issues. He wasn't calling out us. He was calling out the dynamic of the industry as a whole, moving too fast.”Dario Amodei was also asked to put a number on the possibility of AI causing catastrophic harm. He said he used to discuss AI risks in terms of a single probability because it was an easy way to explain the issue. He now believes that approach can hide the different ways AI development could unfold.“I think there's some chance that things go wrong, but, you know, but it's not, it's not all that high,” Amodei said. He then explained that the more useful question is what paths the AI industry takes.“But again, I think it's more illuminating to think in terms of, you know, how do you decompose those probabilities? What are the paths in which things go well, and what are the paths in which things go poorly?”Rather than saying there is a fixed 10% or 20% chance that AI could cause a disaster, Amodei said the outcome depends on decisions made by companies and governments. “And so instead of saying, you know, it's a 10% chance, that sounds like it's a roll of the dice,” he said.He added:“I think it's much more illuminating to say, well, that forks into different paths. And if we take the right path, then the chance of something going wrong is very low. If we take the wrong path, then the chance of something going wrong could be, could be even higher than that.”“So let's focus on our agency, and our ability to take the right paths instead of the wrong paths,” he said.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to Jacob Coxon's resignation. Coxon warned that rapidly developing AI systems could ‘kill us all by the end of the decade’ AmodeI says he agrees with Coxon more than he disagrees with him.

Article Title: Apple bundles TV, Arcade with iCloud+; ends standalone Apple One subscriptions in India
Article Text: Apple is reshaping its subscription business in India. Starting this month, iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost, combining cloud storage, video streaming and gaming in a single subscription.Apple is also introducing Apple Select, a new service integrated into the existing Apple Music app, exclusively for iCloud+ subscribers. This addition extends the expanded bundle’s benefits to the music app, offering subscribers an exclusive collection of music.The expanded service will start at Rs 75 a month for 50GB of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Subscribers can share the package with up to five family members. The rollout will take place through September.The change will end standalone Apple TV and Apple Arcade subscriptions sold directly by Apple in India. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through iCloud+. Apple said access would remain uninterrupted and Arcade game progress and saves would be preserved.Apple One, which bundles several Apple services, will also close to new subscribers in India.Existing subscribers will retain their subscriptions. This means new customers seeking Apple’s combined storage and entertainment offering will be directed towards iCloud+, while current Apple One users can continue with their existing package.Apple One currently has two plans in India: Individual at Rs 195 a month, with 50GB of iCloud+ storage, and Family at Rs 365 a month, with 200GB, shareable with up to five other family members. Both include Apple Music, Apple TV and Apple Arcade. Apple Music is not included in the newly announced iCloud+ bundle, a key distinction for users comparing the offerings.The shift turns cloud storage, often bought when free space runs out, into an entry point for Apple’s entertainment services. For existing iCloud+ customers, the immediate benefit is access to streaming and games without an additional subscription bill.For Apple, bundling could help expose more paying customers to services they may not have chosen separately. It also gives users another reason to retain their storage subscription. However, customers who want only Apple TV or Arcade will now have to take the combined offering when subscribing directly through Apple.“We’re excited to bring Apple TV and Apple Arcade to iCloud+ users in over 100 countries in one convenient subscription,” said Eddy Cue, Apple’s senior vice president of Services and Health.Airtel customers with iPhones can also access the expanded subscription through eligible postpaid plans. Those already receiving Apple TV through select Airtel plans can transition at no additional cost. Availability of individual features, shows and games may vary by country, region or device.
Article Summary: iCloud+ subscribers will get Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no additional cost. The expanded service will start at Rs 75 a month for 50GB of storage, with higher storage tiers also available. Existing individual subscriptions will be cancelled, with users continuing to access the services through iCloud+.

Article Title: In 2013, Marc Benioff wrote a $2.7 million check for schools in San Francisco that Salesforce CEO said was down payment on $100 million; years later one condition remains: Should be no ...
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

Marc Benioff: No conditions for donation schools, except one

Bringing the 1-1-1 model to schools

Salesforce has announced $27 million in new education grants nationwide, including $18 million directly supporting public school districts in San Francisco, Oakland, New York City, Chicago, and Indianapolis. The new funding is said to build on 14 years of partnership with public schools and reflects Salesforce’s continued and growing commitment to supporting schools, educators, and students. Announced ahead of Salesforce’s annual Dreamforce conference, the grants come alongside an expanded focus on education across the company.The latest donation marks the continuation of an effort launched in 2013, when Salesforce CEO and founder Marc Benioff wrote an initial $2.7 million check as a down payment on a decade-long, $100 million pledge. Over the years, Benioff sustained and expanded the initiative, which he claimed represents more funding than any company has given in history and provides consequential support to local public classrooms.Himself a San Francisco resident, in his growing up years, Benioff emphasizes that the money comes without mandates on district policy. He said that the only condition is that there is “no hate, no discrimination” and the grants focus on quality and sustainability.The program pairs capital with direct labor under the company's 1-1-1 philanthropic model, which dedicates 1% each of equity, product, and employee time to charitable causes. Days before the fall term began, high-ranking executives joined staff members on campuses to prepare classrooms.On the latest gift Benioff said, “At Salesforce, we believe business is the greatest platform for change.” He added, “That’s why we created the 1-1-1 model of giving back and built it into our culture from Day One, and it’s why we’ve continued to invest in our communities, in our hometown of San Francisco, and in our public schools for nearly three decades. As AI transforms our world, we have an even greater responsibility to support schools and teachers and help make sure every young person has the opportunity to thrive. The funding historically targeted computer science access and math instruction, but recent disbursements have increasingly addressed the rise of artificial intelligence.
